items.title: PS1 and Xbox Hallmark Christmas Ornaments Are on Sale for Black Friday
items.content_text: If you’re a gamer of a certain age, you may have fond memories of playing the original PlayStation or Xbox consoles. Now you can get gorgeously rendered tiny versions of both classic systems in the form of Christmas ornaments from Hallmark’s Keepsake line. They even light up and make authentic sounds when you press their power buttons. Both ornaments are on sale for under $20 each at Amazon for Black Friday . PlayStation Hallmark Keepsake Ornament The original PlayStation came out in the US in 1994 and has been getting a decent amount of attention lately. LEGO recently turned it into a near 1:1 scale buildable set that I reviewed . This Hallmark ornament PS1 is even closer to the real thing (though much smaller). It’s highly detailed and just beautifully made. When you press the power button the little green light flashes and it plays the iconic PS1 startup sound . The Amazon listing has a video of it. Check it out. Xbox Console - Hallmark Keepsake Ornament The Xbox is just as authentically detailed as the PlayStation. It depicts Microsoft’s black-and-green machine, complete with a Duke controller. Press the power button, and the circle on the front lights up, and it plays the startup sound , followed by the opening music from Halo: Combat Evolved. You can see a video of the process on the Amazon listing . The PS1 normally sells for $29.99, but it’s on sale for $18.80 for Black Friday. That’s only a few cents higher than the all-time low price, not enough to worry about. The Xbox has an MSRP of $27.99, but it’s on sale for $19.60. That’s a new all-time low price. Either way you go, you probably won’t regret the purchase, assuming you have fond memories of playing these consoles in their heyday. I have the SNES ornament, and I love to put it on the tree each year (and press the power button to hear the music from Super Mario World). That one’s currently out of print. I expect these to go out of print as well at some point in the coming years. Grab one now while it’s on sale if you want it. items.title: After Playing Infinity Nikki 3.0 for Four Hours, its New Cities and Outfits Are Just Some of the Additions Worth Returning For
items.excerpt: The new 3.0 update has tons of new stuff to explore including new locations, outfits and gameplay systems, although don't expect any kind of proper challenge.
items.content_text: When Infinity Nikki first launched in 2024, it introduced players around the world to the dress-up world of mobile game star Nikki in her first 3D console/PC adventure, an open world filled with wholesome fun, fashion and friendship. 2025’s V2.0 update introduced a new area to the world of Miraland, as well as new ways to traverse it. But now with the new V3.0 update titled Of Yesterday and Tomorrow, Nikki’s wonderful world has been expanded significantly – with its richest locations yet, and even a cute convertible to traverse it with. To give you an idea of how huge this update is, I played for over four hours at developer Infold’s Shanghai office, focusing mainly on story content and with only the slightest bit of open-world exploration and lifestyle simulation gameplay, and didn't even see all of one of its two new cities. The golden path apparently offers some nine hours of story content, with two dense and exciting new areas to get lost in. Between the V3.0 launch and Nikki’s birthday celebration campaign, players can get 160 free draws and 19 new sets of clothing. I spent most of my time in Cicia, a city of art, based loosely on Paris among other places, and lined with cobblestone streets and beatific brickwork architecture. Cicia was previously featured as a location in the mobile game Shining Nikki, and makes its 3D debut here. It’s a world where art nouveau, belle epoque and art deco collide, and home to the Cicia Art Academy where Miraland’s most promising students are taught lessons of art creation and appraisal by the finest tutors. When Nikki receives an invitation to study there, she and her catlike companion Momo embark on a new adventure of aesthetic discovery. But is everything at the academy truly as it seems? Some of the outfits in the update grant Nikki new skills. Unlock and craft the preppy four-star Leaping Breeze outfit to gain a higher double-jump and airborne dash abilities, while the much darker and sexier Night’s Hidden Side outfit allows Nikki to “bind” with objects around the environment (think Mario’s possession skill in Mario Odyssey) and use them to warp to hard-to-reach places. These new skills allow for a new level of verticality in Cicia’s map and dungeons, helping you explore the castle spires or negotiate intricate dungeon maps. You can also find a musket for long-range attacks (which is a new Whimtech item), and dress for the occasion in Cicia’s three-star, nine-piece outfit Song of Endless Youth. V3.0 also introduces a new outfit category, Star Crown Resonance. The Star Crown Resonance outfit named Where Stars Shine Again comes with a musket and staff, and is designed for tougher combat situations. With either weapon equipped, Nikki’s unused dashes are stored, and you can release them all at once or use them one at a time, creating a sort of combo system that deals more damage. While previous Infinity Nikki maps tended towards countryside locations, Cicia is a bustling city. Arriving by airship to take in the stunning views, Nikki and Momo step into a throng of students, teachers and residents, each with voiced dialogue to idly eavesdrop on as they prepare for a huge school festival, building an air of excitement as Nikki starts academy life. In this maelstrom of culture, recruiters for the drama club and literature club compete for Nikki’s attention. And then she meets Béatrice Laviolette. A young ducal heiress, at first Béatrice is quite brusque, standoffish and snobby. It started to feel like meeting Glinda in the heightened magical environs of Shiz University, and when it was announced in a cutscene that the students would compete for the right to wear a legendary Miracle Outfit, I assumed Nikki and Béatrice were heading into a bitter rivalry. But Nikki has always been a relentlessly positive character, with a deep and forgiving heart and a desire to encourage those around her. Without wanting to spoil anything, let’s just say that she, Béatrice and earnest classmate Déphine Garnier foster a relationship that may surprise you. Meanwhile, fellow student Sikong Ran invites Nikki to join his Society of Whispers and Wonders, a supernatural-obsessed group who study things that go boo in the night – lending more than a little taste of Wednesday or Riverdale high-school mystery. Exploring the city is a reward unto itself. Rich and bustling with life, it features picturesque sunsets, glittering lakes, colourful flowerbeds, gargling fountains. It is filled with side missions and simple minigames, including one where you construct a street band to perform jolly jazz music in the castle plaza. In the streets, teachers guide students through artistic concepts that are interesting to read – for example, did you know that in music, technical perfection is no match for the heart of the musician? The characters you meet are endearing; and as before, the dialogue is filled with gentle humour – not least the central relationship between Nikki and Momo, which remains as heartwarming as ever. But as you progress, Nikki learns that behind the magic of this idyllic city, there is a dark secret. Using her new binding skill to unravel environmental puzzles, she is drawn into a conspiracy that only Nikki can solve. As part of this, I got to play through one of two new dungeons, titled The Ideal City. This is a clockwork house of tricks that recalls the steampunk-coded vibe of earlier Infinity Nikki dungeons, with huge cogs that alter the mechanical environments as they turn, and wooden theatre dioramas folding in and out of view in the background as you progress. Half of the exploration takes the form of platforming action, which, like previous Infinity Nikki dungeons, is not exactly a tough challenge, but enough to make use of Nikki’s new jump and dash abilities and test your reactions a little. The other half is made up of environmental puzzles that use Nikki’s new bind ability, tasking you with scanning the area of objects to possess and manipulate in order to progress – for example, turning keys or bouncing between bird-shaped statues on high-up ledges. In one section, you even possess a giant glass marble and manoeuvre it along tight, narrow ledges, like Super Monkey Ball. The variety of gameplay on offer is strong, and, combined with the fantastic art design and hummable jazzy soundtrack, makes up for the lack of a tougher challenge. Speaking of which, I also got to try a boss battle from later in the campaign, making use of Nikki’s battle-ready Where Stars Shine Again outfit for more powerful combos. I was able to beat the boss on my first try. But Infinity Nikki isn’t really supposed to be a hardcore action experience, and the drama of the scene and the story beats that lead up to it should satisfy fans, while offering some mild challenge to younger players. Also in Cicia, I got to try the new driving system. Up until now, Nikki has largely travelled on foot or by bicycle, but now she has a range of vehicles to choose from – and fun ways to use them. You can get your own convertible, pay in-game currency to rent a classic car, and unlock even more. While driving, you can change the radio stations like in GTA, engage in Uber-style mini-missions like in Crazy Taxi, or simply drive to your destination. The car even has a jump button. But what impressed me the most is how photo mode has been integrated here. Infinity Nikki has had a strong photo mode since launch, allowing players to dress and pose Nikki and Momo to their satisfaction and snap them at will. I wondered if it would work while she was in the driver’s seat – and I was pleasantly surprised to find that not only does it work, it comes with a wealth of car-specific customisation options – such as opening or closing the doors, switching the head lamps on or off, and raising or lowering the convertible roof. These thoughtful touches enhanced my time spent with Nikki on the road, and show just how much care and attention have gone into this new update. Did I mention that Cicia is only one of two new areas? I spent just a little bit of time in Ceremius, a city with more of a dark fantasy style. Here a terrible earthquake has upended the city, while some magical force has held it together in surreal ways. But while the post-disaster atmosphere is undoubtedly more sombre and intense than in Cicia, the city is still densely populated with residents. The art theme also remains, with a plethora of statues and installations to find. Clicking on one bizarre statue, I got a paragraph of smartly written critique, explaining the work with the eye of an art collector. Ceremius also features a new set of alchemy abilities, which I didn't have time to try, but promise to add even more depth to an already packed content update. During my time with Of Yesterday and Tomorrow, it was a pleasure to return to Nikki’s fashion-friendly world. In particular, Cicia and Ceremius are introduced in impressive detail, and I felt like I was not only exploring a real place, but enjoying the design team’s eye for art as well, as the story presents artworks, fashion and musical theatre in a way that actually lets you experience them directly. The update drops today, so jump in and dress up to see for yourself. Daniel Robson is the Executive Producer of IGN Japan.
items.title_en: After Playing Infinity Nikki 3.0 for Four Hours, its New Cities and Outfits Are Just Some of the Additions Worth Returning For

items.title: Lucia Actress Manni L. Perez Issues First Statement Since GTA 6 Launch
items.excerpt: Manni L. Perez, the actress who plays Lucia in GTA 6, has issued her first statement since the game came out.
items.content_text: Manni L. Perez, the actress who plays Lucia in GTA 6 , has issued her first statement since the game came out. Perez’s role as Lucia Caminos was confirmed when she was nominated in the Best Performance category for this year’s The Game Awards , a day before GTA 6 launched on November 19. She’s now considered the favorite following the game’s critically acclaimed, record-breaking launch. Now, a week later, Perez took to social media to thank fans for the reception to GTA 6. “Life has been such a whirlwind these past couple of days and I just want to take a moment to say thank you,” an Instagram Stories post began. “Thank you to all the new followers, to all the beautiful messages, and the positive reception the game and my character have received. “I've dedicated almost a decade bringing Lucia to life. She's been such a significant part of mine and I am beyond grateful she now gets to be a small part of yours.” “Happy Holiday's y'all.” Perez is an actress with a smattering of credits to her acting resume, including TV guest roles in Jessica Jones, Chicago P.D., and Law & Order: Special Victims Unit. While she hasn't been up to much else over the past few years, it's easy to know why — GTA 6 sounds like it was a pretty involved project. Indeed, Lucia isn’t Perez's first GTA role. In GTA 5, she plays the background character of "Clubber #2," while in GTA Online she voices a blackjack dealer. Meanwhile, Jason actor Dylan Rourke also posted a message of gratitude on Instagram Stories, saying: “Thankful for this wild ride. Gratitude won’t cut it. Make today about the ones you love.” Manni L. Perez shouldn't be confused with Manny Perez, who plays Raul Bautista in GTA 6. This week, Manny Perez bought a PS5 just so he could play the game, saying in a video posted to social media: “Guy, I’m playing and this s**t is crazy! Look how real that looks. I’m learning, I’m loving this, it’s crazy.” Other GTA 6 actors who've started to talk about their work on the game include Lexie Shoaibi, who recently spoke out about her "bittersweet" newfound fame after her character, Mandy, went viral online, and Cocoteo FM radio host Issa Lopez, who described the wild non-disclosure agreement she had to sign before working on the game . Last month, the actors behind GTA 5's Franklin, Michael, and Trevor shared their advice for GTA 6's cast in a bid to ready them for the kind of fame few video game actors achieve. items.title: GTA 6 Fashion in the IGN Community
items.content_text: It’s hard to believe it’s only been seven days since the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 . Still, with the staggering number of screenshots, videos, and everything else filling up social media feeds, anyone out of the loop would never know. I think much of this is due to just how many types of games Rockstar managed to cram into GTA 6. Everything from fixing up Jason’s house in the prologue to racing, billiards, birdwatching , and, of course, all the other gameplay we expect in GTA has created an almost Sims-like experience that is getting more people than ever to try the series. Seriously, though, the early sales numbers are bonkers. My and many others' favorite things about GTA 6, in addition to just being a general menace to society, have been experiencing all the different kinds of gameplay and Rockstar fitting into it. I’ve been checking in with our IGN community across our various platforms to see how their time in Leonida has been going. I’m still gathering stories for that (If you’re interested in sharing your thoughts, join the IGN Discord); however, in the meantime, I wanted to share the fashion that various members of the IGN Community and Staff have for Jason and Lucia as they make their way through the story. items.title: Alienware Makes Some of the Best OLED Gaming Monitors Around and They're All on Sale for Black Friday
items.excerpt: Backed by a 3 year warranty that covers OLED burn-in.
items.content_text: Alienware OLED gaming monitors are the best displays that you can get for your PC. I currently own and use high-end monitors from several brands, but my favorite monitor thus far is a 39" Alienware 5K OLED monitor. Alienware sources its OLED panels from Samsung and LG and then adds on a 3 year warranty that covers burn-in. For Black Friday , most of Dell's newest 2026 and 2025 monitors have dropped to new price lows and are, in general, more affordable than equivalent Samsung and LG models. Black Friday Alienware OLED Gaming Monitor Deals During this Black Friday season, get an additional 2X back in Dell rewards with every monitor purchase. You will need to sign up for a Dell Rewards membership, which is free to join. 39" Alienware AW3926QW 5K RGB Tandem Stripe OLED Monitor Earlier this year, Dell announced the "world's first 39" 5K monitor with RGB stripe tandem OLED technology."It launched with a retail price of $1,099.99 but for Black Friday you can get it for $100 less . The Alienware AW3926QW has no lack of features that make it stand out from the crowd, but perhaps its most impressive inclusion is the LG RGB stripe tandem OLED panel. Tandem OLED stacks multiple OLED layers on top of each other instead of a single layer. Tandem OLED is better than other OLED panels because: 1) it's much brighter (the AW3926QW in particular has a very impressive 1,300 nits of peak brightness) and 2) it's less prone to burn-in. The AW3926QW doubles down on this with new RGB stripe technology. Whereas traditional tandem OLEDs use white pixels, RGB stripe tandem OLED breaks the color down further into vertically aligned red, green, and blue pixels. This reduces color fringing and in turn significantly improves text clarity. It goes without saying that there are obvious benefits here for both gaming and productivity purposes alike. 32" Alienware AW3226Q 4K RGB Tandem Stripe OLED Monitor The 32" Alienware AW3226Q gaming monitor is another recent release that's aimed toward the more budget-conscious crowd. The monitor launched about a month ago at a very reasonable $699.99 price tag, but it's already $150 off for Black Friday. Unlike the slighty more expensive AW3225QF which uses a curved 240Hz QD-OLED panel from Samsung, the Alienware AW3226Q is equipped with a flat panel 165Hz RGB stripe tandem OLED panel from LG. In exchange for a lower refresh rate and no official G-Sync certification (it's still G-Sync compatible), you get better text clarity and arguably a better monitor for non-gaming use. 32" Alienware AW3225QF 4K 240Hz QD-OLED Gaming Monitor Alienware's most popular 4K OLED gaming monitor is also down to its lowest price ever. For Black Friday, you can pick up a 32" Alienware AW3225QF 4K QD OLED gaming monitor for just $699.99 with free shipping. The AW3225QF is a rare gaming monitor that combines a native 4K resolution, 240Hz refresh rate , and a gorgeous Samsung-sourced quantum dot OLED panel. If you're looking for the best 4K gaming monitor , this should definitely be on your short list. The Alienware AW3225QF is HDR True Black 400 certified with up to 1,000 nits of peak brightness. It also boasts a factory calibrated 99.3% DCI-P3 color range, 1700R curve, and G-Sync certification . 27" Alienware AW2726DM QHD QD-OLED Gaming Monitor Most people would agree that OLED monitors are as good as it gets for gaming. items.title: Microsoft-Owned GitHub Stuns Followers as It Celebrates AnyPS5 Repo in Now-Deleted Tweet
items.excerpt: In a post that’s since been deleted, Microsoft-owned code and software collaboration site GitHub celebrated the AnyPS5 repo “passing 58k stars” from users on the platform as a result of the launch of GTA 6. items.content_text: In a post that’s since been deleted, Microsoft-owned code and software collaboration site GitHub celebrated the AnyPS5 repo “passing 58k stars” from users on the platform as a result of the launch of GTA 6. GitHub even told followers "Happy GTA VImas!" in a tweet that will almost certainly have infurated Rockstar Games, parent company Take-Two, PlayStation, and Xbox. “GTA 6 is finally here, sparking one of the biggest weeks in gaming and open source on GitHub,” the post said, before jumping into celebrating the repo. “Does changing where games run cross a legal line?” the tweet asked. This is insane https://t.co/mwU6VIy1nI — MVG (@ModernVintageG) November 26, 2026 There was also an official video attached to the tweet, which highlighted a post from an AnyPS5 coder, via Kotaku . The post in the video said: “We have 3 days until GTA 6 everyone[…]get your agents or deevs[sic] and work.” While the post could easily be the work of a rogue social media person, the optics aren’t good at all. GTA 6 is only officially available on PS5 and Xbox Series X and S, so both Sony and Microsoft have benefited greatly from the game's record-breaking launch. To see a the Microsoft-owned GitHub post a message to its followers essentially encouraging potential piracy is remarkable. IGN has asked for comment, but GitHub obviously realized its mistake — it deleted the tweet, after all — but how it even got approved in the first place is a mystery until the company comments. Take-Two is currently working to take down various homebrew community efforts from GitHub, as the race to release an unofficial GTA 6 PC port heats up. This follows Cyberleek's alleged released of the executable file for the incomplete GTA 6 Xbox build they reportedly leaked the week prior. There’s even a website tracking the various attempts to recompile, emulate, or port the leaked Xbox Series build to PC. The big question for Take-Two is, can it do anything meaningful to stop a working, playable build of GTA 6 on PC from getting into people's hands? GitHub takedowns can only go so far, as the homebrew scenes uses AI to speed along development. Take-Two stands to make billions of dollars more from the official PC release of GTA 6, so any unofficial version is a significant business risk. In a recent interview with IGN sister site RPS , former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij said that Rockstar Games may be keen to port GTA 6 to PC as soon as possible , due to the explosion of AI-generated clones and ports. It's also worth noting that there is extra interest in a PC version of GTA 6 because the console versions target 30fps. The PC version, resumably, will run at 60fps or whatever frame rate your rig is capable of . Earlier this month, Strauss Zelnick, the boss of Take-Two, responded to the threat of AI-assisted reverse-engineering and decompilation of games in an interview with IGN. He said he was taking the issue seriously, and insisted that fans will prefer to play GTA 6 officially, with all its bells and whistles as Rockstar intended, over an unofficial PC version. Here’s the exchange: IGN: We've seen hackers using AI to clone games much faster than ever before, even try to jailbreak consoles. And there is some concern about this leading to potentially GTA 6 being made available on PC unofficially or places that you aren't releasing it. I was just wondering how much of a threat this is to your business? And, is there anything meaningful you can do about it? Strauss Zelnick: I don't think it’s a financial matter, in terms of a threat to our business. I do think it’s a creative matter. It's important to everyone, our developers and our consumers alike, to deliver the experience Rockstar envisions. And at the same time, of course, we protect our intellectual property vigilantly. So we are focused on these concerns. We're not in the least cavalier about them. Technology is advancing quickly. And at the same time, I do think that pretty much everyone wants the Rockstar experience as Rockstar intended. IGN: Related, last week Anthropic confirmed they took steps to block Claude from reverse engineering video games. I would assume you would welcome that. And would you like to see other AI companies like OpenAI do the same thing to prevent people from using these powerful AI models to clone your games? Strauss Zelnick: I think all companies should be protecting intellectual property, their own and everyone else's. And if you're in the intellectual property business, which Anthropic is and OpenAI is, then it seems ironic on the one hand to stomp on someone else's IP and hope that yours is protected. During an investor-focused Q&A following the release of Take-Two’s latest financial report, attended by IGN, Zelnick was asked multiple times about the AI reverse-engineering problem. He, again, had strong words in response, suggesting Take-Two was ready to lawyer up. “This business has been largely immune to piracy concerns forever because of file sizes, complexity of piracy, being connected to servers and the like,” he began. “And undoubtedly, it would be very difficult to replicate the experience of consuming our game as intended because of technical limitations. “That said, it's going to become more of a challenge, as you said, and we're aware of that. So we are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defenses and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And at the same time, without in any way being cavalier, every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy. So this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it.” Zelnick’s talk about legal activities sparks an obvious question: what can game companies do about AI-assisted reverse engineering? It's a question IGN recently asked when people started to work on a PC port of Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake . If you're still getting your bearings, discover GTA's new systems with the Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , or get all the details on the first chapters with the Chapter 1 Guide and Tips , Chapter 2 Guide and Tips , and Chapter 3 Guide and Tips . items.content_text: Last year, Hisense pioneered the first RGB Mini-LED TV with its 116UX model. Granted it was only available as a massive 116" screen that retailed for $20,000. In 2026, Hisense released its second generation RGB Mini-LED tech at a much more affordable price point with its UR-series lineup. For Black Friday, you can get it for even less. Best Buy has just discounted the 65" Hisense UR8 RGB Mini-LED TV from $2,000 all the way down to $899.99 and the 75" model from $2,500 down to $1399.99, both with free delivery. These are the lowest prices since launch and beats previous lows by $200. The Hisense UR8 RGB Mini-LED TV Gives OLED a Run for Its Money RGB Mini-LED is essentially the next generation evolution of Mini-LED technology. Traditional mini-LED TVs consist of an array of blue LED that are passed through RGB filters to produced the desired color. RGB Mini-LED TVs use red, green, and blue LEDs instead of just blue, which means the pixels no longer need filters to produce the desired color. The result is more accurate color reproduction, less blooming and, most importantly, a wider color gamut. In fact, the color gamut of RGB Mini-LED surpasses that of OLEDs, since current-generation OLEDs also use color filters combined with blue OLEDs. How does that translate in the real world? It means that you see richer, more accurate colors, smoother gradients and less banding than even OLEDs, especially in 4K HDR content. RGB Mini-LED TVs have several other features that out-class standard Mini-LEDs. They're brighter (far brighter than OLED TVs), making them perfect for daytime watching in bright rooms with little light control. They offer much better viewing angles, which means everyone you're hosting will enjoy the game wherever they're positioned around the TV. Gamers will benefit from this TV as well. The Hisense UR8 boasts a 180Hz native refresh rate, the highest I've ever seen for a TV, with HDMI 2.1 inputs that will pair seamlessly with a PlayStation 5 console for seamlessly running games in 4K. items.title: Chainsaws 'Would Have Been Too Much' Even for GTA 6, as Rockstar Explains Why Some Extra Violent Weapons Are Missing
items.excerpt: Rockstar has explained why some extra violent weapons like chainsaws and katanas are missing from GTA 6.
items.content_text: You can commit an extreme amount of violence in GTA 6 , with a wide variety of weaponry. Guns, baseball bats, even tanks can be your chosen tool of destruction. But that hasn’t stopped some from wondering where some series favourites have disappeared to. Among those are the likes of katanas and chainsaws, which were staples during Grand Theft Auto’s “3D universe” games, including Vice City and San Andreas. The chainsaw, in particular, holds a special connection to Vice City given its clear Scarface inspirations, and memorable scene involving the power tool from the 1983 movie. But despite some being spotted around the latest version of Leonida in GTA 6, neither Jason nor Lucia can wield them as weapons. Why? Well, Rockstar co-studio head Rob Nelson explained the decision in an interview with VGC . “As far as the chainsaw — I think it would have been too much for this game at this resolution and these characters,” Nelson says. "It’s not a resource thing. Even at the most psycho, did Jason and Lucia really need that — what’s that going to look like?” When asked specifically about why chainsaws are lying about the world, but can’t be picked up, Nelson explained that, “you’re always trying to find what is the right sort of line and the right balance; it really just depends — you want to feel like you can interact with as much of the world as possible.” I have to somewhat agree that it just wouldn’t feel like it fit either Jason or Lucia’s characters to be roaming around looking for limbs to chop off with a mechanised serrated blade. Ultimately, their story is one about committing crime to escape to a better, more “normal” life, not one about two psychopaths with a lust for blood going on a rampage. That being said, when whatever the online component of GTA 6 launches, I could see objects like this becoming weapons, allowing for people to roleplay as whatever brand of criminal, psychopath, or tree sculptor they wish. There’s a world of possibilities out there. Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? Check out the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide right here on IGN. If you're still getting your bearings, discover GTA's new systems with the Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , or get all the details on the first chapters with the Chapter 1 Guide and Tips , Chapter 2 Guide and Tips , and Chapter 3 Guide and Tips . items.content_text: Update Nov 26, 7pm ET: Stock is now gone for all of these games. There's a chance Walmart will get more codes once Black Friday actually rolls around. I'll update this page if so. Here's some excellent news for anyone with a Switch or Switch 2: the Nintendo Black Friday deals are incredibly strong this year. Stronger than ever, really. Nintendo is known as a company that barely ever runs discounts, and when it does, they're pretty weak compared to other game makers. This year, though, retailers like Amazon and Walmart are taking the lead and dropping prices incredibly low. To wit: four digital Switch and Switch 2 games just dropped to $30 at Walmart. We're talking Donkey Kong Bananza, Kirby Air Riders, and more. Let's take a look. The games in question are the Nintendo Switch 2 games Donkey Kong Bananza, Kirby Air Riders, Super Mario Party Jamboree + Jamboree TV, and the original Switch compilation Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2. That last one is a port of the 3D Mario classics from the Wii generation, if you can remember that far back. All of these games are well worth the $30 price tag. Donkey Kong Bananza was made by the same team behind the stunning Switch platformer Super Mario Odyssey. We gave Donkey Kong Bananza a 10/10 score in our review , with critic Logan Plant writing, "Donkey Kong Bananza is a truly groundbreaking 3D platformer, with satisfying movement, powerful abilities, impressive destructible environments, and clever challenges that all come together in complete harmony to create Nintendo’s first Switch 2 masterpiece." Kirby Air Riders, meanwhile, is an often-overlooked racer from the minds behind Super Smash Bros. Logan Plant gave it an 8/10 in our review , writing, "Kirby Air Riders' unconventional controls can get in its own way sometimes, but they don't stop it from being a fun, frantic action racing game with an almost unreal amount of stuff to do." In our review , (once again) Logan Plant wrote, "Super Mario Party Jamboree itself is still fantastic, but the mixed new content of the Switch 2 Edition + Jamboree TV re-release adds frustrating limitations and strange design decisions to what was otherwise a polished, customizable experience." Still, for $30, it's well worth it. And as for the Mario Galaxy collection? We didn't give it a straight-up review since mostly just direct ports of the Wii originals, but with controls that work better on Switch. It's a terrific pair of games that play great on Switch or Switch 2. It's unclear how much digital stock Walmart has for these games. And at this Black Friday price, it's likely to go fast. items.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Rerelease Includes a Scene Cut From Avengers: Doomsday
items.excerpt: Spider-Man: Brand New Day rerelease includes a scene cut from Avengers: Doomsday, according to a new report.
items.content_text: Spider-Man: Brand New Day rerelease includes a scene cut from Avengers: Doomsday , according to a new report. The New York Times published an article on the potential for the release of Avengers: Doomsday and Dune: Part 3 — dubbed DunesDay by fans — to set box office records, and within it is a tease for the extra footage set to be included in Spider-Man: Brand New Day’s return to theaters. According to the NYT, Spider-Man: Brand New Day will have a scene cut from Doomsday added to the end of the movie as a bonus. We don’t know what’s in the scene, but it’s meant to serve as an ad for the upcoming MCU film. Spider-Man: Brand New Day made an eye-watering $2.5 billion at the global box office, so I assume you've seen it. If so, has the promise of a new Avengers: Doomsday scene convinced you to double-dip? Let us know in the comments! What we know for sure is that Rosario Dawson will return as Claire Temple in the rerelease , marking her long-awaited comeback to the MCU. Warning! Spoilers for Spider-Man: Brand New Day follow. Last week, Dawson revealed a photo of her in costume for her first Marvel appearance in a decade, standing in nurse scrubs next to Tom Holland's Spider-Man. It's a scene that fans thought they'd never get to see after it was deleted from the final cut of the movie . Now, however, it is being reinstated for the film's extended edition rerelease , entitled Spider-Man: [Brand New] Brand New Day, alongside a handful of other moments previously left on the cutting room floor. It's pretty obvious when this scene will take place, as Dawson's character stands next to Tom Holland's Spider-Man who is wearing a hospital gown and his Spidey mask. Of course, Spider-Man finds himself in hospital towards the end of the movie, and Dawson's return will likely answer fan questions surrounding how the superhero got patched up with no one else discovering his identity. (The answer, surely, is that Dawson takes care of him directly — having been used to keeping numerous superhero identities secret in the past.) Spider-Man: Brand New Day returns to theaters on December 4, 2026, now with Rosario Dawson and an Avengers: Doomsday cut scene included. Avengers: Doomsday itself launches on December 18. Today, we got our first look at Magneto vs Doom in a new teaser for Avengers: Doomsday.
